paperName: The Operation of Markets and Market Failure

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes the basic economic problem?

options.text: Living standards are low for many people
Resources are being depleted too rapidly
Resources are scarce relative to needs and wants
Resources are unequally distributed

questions.questionText: A rise in the price of blueberries from £8 to £10 per kg encourages growers to increase their supply from 12 kg to 21 kg each week. Other things remaining the same, this suggests that the price elasticity of supply for blueberries is

The following diagram shows the free market supply (S) and demand (D1) for a good when there is imperfect information. D2 shows the level of demand if consumers had full information about the effects of consuming the good. Which one of the following government policies is most likely to result in the social optimum level of consumption?

options.text: A maximum price equal to P3
A minimum price equal to P2
A subsidy per unit equal to P1 – P2
A tax per unit equal to P3 – P2

questions.questionText: Firms in the steel industry in an economy move abroad to where costs are lower. The redundant steel workers are occupationally immobile. This situation represents a market failure because

options.text: domestic steel production is replaced by imported steel.
some factors of production will not be fully employed.
there is no government provision of training schemes.
there will be underproduction of a merit good.

questions.questionText: A government plans to build a new road to bypass a small town. The table below shows the costs and benefits of two possible routes for the new road. questions.questionText: The market for crab sandwiches experiences an increase in the price and an increase in the output of crab sandwiches. Which of the following combinations of events is the only one that could have caused these changes?

options.text: A fall in the price of tuna sandwiches and a fall in the price of crab
A new tax on food packaging and a fall in labour productivity
A rise in the price of prawn sandwiches and a rise in the price of bread
New entry of firms into the sandwich market and a reduction in the minimum wage

questions.questionText: A construction firm uses workers, machines and raw materials to build new houses. One year the firm builds 20 more houses than in the previous year. It can be concluded that there must have been an increase in

options.text: employment.
production.
productive efficiency.
productivity.

questions.questionText: The following supply and demand diagram shows the impact of a government tax on chocolate bars. The amount of tax revenue raised each week is

options.text: £0.45 million
£0.60 million
£0.75 million
£1.00 million

questions.questionText: Two large firms dominate the market for manufacturing rail track. This means that

options.text: abuse of monopoly power will result in diseconomies of scale.
barriers to entry are low as neither firm is a pure monopoly.
neither firm has monopoly power but benefits from economies of scale.
the two firms have monopoly power but may also compete.

questions.questionText: A clothes retailer has experimented with changing the prices of various items of clothing sold in their shop. The table below shows the different prices per item in 2 years. Other things being equal, which one of the following changes from Year 1 to Year 2 is the retailer most likely to experience?

options.text: A decrease in revenue from socks if the price elasticity of demand is minus one
A decrease in revenue from T-shirts if the price elasticity of demand is elastic
An increase in revenue from trainers if the price elasticity of demand is inelastic
An increase in revenue from trousers if the price elasticity of demand is elastic

questions.questionText: The benefit one person obtains from breathing clean air does not reduce the benefits other people can obtain from the clean air. This characteristic represents

options.text: non-excludability of a public good.
non-rivalry of a public good.
optimum provision of a public good.
the free-rider problem of a public good.

questions.questionText: The following table shows the price of spaghetti in 3 years. Over the 3 years, it can be concluded that there has been a fall in

options.text: the average cost of producing spaghetti.
the average revenue from sale of spaghetti.
the consumer demand for spaghetti.
the total revenue from sale of spaghetti.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a true statement about market structures? Market structures

options.text: are partly defined by the number of firms in the market.
are the rules imposed by governments which limit how firms behave.
include concentrated markets but not competitive markets.
include markets for goods but not markets for services.

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows demand and supply in the market for roses. The demand for roses shifts from D1 to D2. Other things remaining the same, it can be concluded that

options.text: monopoly suppliers have pushed up the price of roses.
the higher price of roses will cause demand to fall back to D1.
the income elasticity of demand for roses is positive.
there is greater incentive to supply roses.

questions.questionText: A government sets a maximum price below the current market price for rented housing. The likely long-run consequence is that

options.text: fewer people can live in rented housing.
the rationing function of prices will improve.
there will be a fall in supply of owner-occupied housing.
there will be excess supply of rented housing.

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the long-run average cost curve (LRAC) for a firm. From the diagram it can be concluded that

options.text: average fixed costs will fall and then rise.
economies of scale are present at some levels of output.
the firm will inevitably experience diseconomies of scale.
total costs must first fall and then rise.

questions.questionText: ‘Large pay bonuses received by top executives have caused income inequality to increase.’ This statement

options.text: is an example of a normative statement.
is an example of an hypothesis that can be tested.
shows that income tax is not sufficiently progressive.
shows that the distribution of income is inequitable.

questions.questionText: An economy produces racing cars and robots. The economy’s initial production possibility frontier (PPF1) is shown in the diagram below. The economy’s production possibility frontier shifts to PPF2 and as a result of this change the

options.text: number of racing cars that can be produced for each robot given up has increased.
opportunity cost of producing robots is now lower.
output of racing cars will be higher than the output of robots.
productive efficiency of producing robots has risen.
